blind.why: Long seen from Long Doors (38,0,30) against Inferno Banana. Ours frames the lane well with the arch, depth and a landmark tower, but the floor is flat sand, the 'LONG DOORS' callout is white-on-sand and nearly unreadable, and nothing under the arch is lit. The ref has warm bounce under the arch, string lights and a painted B marker. It has more hierarchy and a clearer read.

B Site from Tunnel Mouth (-33,-0.7,-16) against the Inferno market pergola. Our 'lantern-market pergola' reads as bare dark gallows posts with a few cube fruits, and the backdrop is a flat brick wall with repeated windows. The ref pergola is a dense, lit hero piece that anchors the space.

Upper Tunnel (-33,0,0) looking south against a CS2 covered canal passage. Ours now has value contrast, but the ceiling is a black void, the hanging lamps are white cubes that light nothing, and the murals read as blank white triangles. The ref glows with warm bounce, and the enemy silhouette pops against the bright exit.

A Site from the Ledge (45,3.6,-40) against Mirage A through a window. Ours is a noisy skyline of six towers over a low-contrast floor 'A', with small scattered cover. The ref has a framed, legible site layout, a painted A, and cover with clear silhouettes.

biggest_gap: Local light does not exist. All 125 lamps are unlit emissive white cubes, and the round-4 'floor light pools' cannot be seen at eye height, so covered spaces read as flat dark voids with floating white squares rather than as lit interiors. Reproduce in a live match (?test=1&seed=3&match=1&phase=live) with place(-39,0,22) looking north into Lower Tunnel / Tunnel Bend, place(-33,0,0) looking south into Upper Tunnel, or place(0,0,-30) looking at the Tide Mid fountain lantern plinths, which are plain white boxes. The floor under every lamp is the same dark brick as the floor between lamps, and the ceilings are pure black. In CS2 (Banana arch, Mirage connector, the Inferno pergola) every lamp throws a visible warm pool on the floor and walls about 3-4 m across, and shaded walls get warm sun bounce, so a covered lane has light and dark rhythm and players stand out against it. To fix: bake or add real light pools (radius 3-4 m, clearly brighter floor and walls under each lamp), add a light cone or glow halo to the lamp heads, give tunnel ceilings a lit gradient instead of black, and add warm bounce to shaded facades and arch undersides.
other_gaps: Signature pieces are thin. The B pergola (-33,-1.4,-28) and the A gazebo are bare posts and a roof, with cube fruit and no string lights or density, so they do not read as hero landmarks at eye height the way Inferno's market or Mirage's palace do.

Surfaces repeat. The same cracked-plaster/brick patch decal is stamped on almost every wall (Tide Spawn, Ember Mid, B Window, Pit), and facades are large blank planes with grid windows, so the material identity per region comes almost entirely from hue.

Floor callouts have poor contrast. 'LONG DOORS' (38,0,28) and the site 'A'/'B' floor marks are pale on pale paving and hard to read at 10 m. CS2 uses high-contrast painted wall letters at eye height instead.

The spawns mirror each other. Ember Mid (0,0,36 -> 'FLUX MARKET' kiosk) and Tide Spawn (0,0,-44 -> 'CAFE LUNA' kiosk) have the same composition (kiosk blocking the lane, bunting, arch behind), which weakens orientation.
The A site skyline is noisy. From the Ledge, six towers and a crowd of rooftops compete with the site, while the cover pieces are small and lack clear silhouettes.

The map is compact. Measured with the real movement sim, Ember reaches A in 11.5 s (Long) or 14.1 s (Short) and B in 12.1-12.8 s, while Tide reaches A in 4.9 s and B in 5.5 s. Rotations take 9.2 s (Palace) or 10.3-10.5 s (via Tide Spawn). Bot first contact averages 21 s. Timings are balanced, but the lanes are short for the 105 s round.
bugs: The map path 'rotate-b-to-a-palace' is not walkable. Its waypoints step from (16.5,0,-26) to (18.5,3.0,-27), a 3 m rise onto Terrace with no jump allowed. Driving the real movement sim along it (forward held, yaw toward each next waypoint) gets the actor stuck at (16.6,0,-25.6) after 9.0 s. The reverse path 'rotate-a-to-b-palace' completes in 9.2 s. The doc claims paths are 'walkable without jumping'.

There is a floor shading seam on Long Ramp. Seen from (38,0.38,-6) looking toward (35,-28), a hard-edged lighter vertical strip about 1 m wide runs straight across the paving to the horizon at screen x of about 715 px, cutting through tile joints. It looks like a vertex-colour/AO cell boundary, not a shadow.
strengths: The tunnels now have real value contrast and four distinct identities per bend: teal tile, red brick, whitewash/blue, and terracotta.
The landmarks work: the clock tower, the teal A dome and the campanile are visible from most areas and aid orientation.

Layout and timing work. Sim walks of 9 of 10 paths found no snags, and a 107-point random-walk stress test found no fall-through from legitimate positions. An all-bot match ran 4 rounds with 0 stuck incidents, 0 teleports and 0 exceptions, and split 2-2.
The arches over Long and Mid frame the sightlines well, and the kiosk breaks the spawn-to-spawn peek.
Performance is reasonable: 97-137 draw calls and about 185-195k tris at eye height across 22 views, with no console errors.
